a secret code that proves to an outside service that the app is allowed to use it
the address and login details the app uses to reach its database

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Template of required settings
sections.what: Lists the settings the app needs: a database address, the AI provider choice, two API keys, and the two model names. Secret values are left blank.
sections.why: Likely reason: shows the names needed without exposing any real secret.
sections.watch_out: Do not put real keys in this file, because it is meant to be shared.

summary: A template that lists the environment settings the app expects, with blank values for secrets and a set of model names for AI document extraction.
purpose: Shows a developer which settings to create in a real environment file.
why: Likely reason: lists required setting names without storing any real secret in the code.
how: Copy the file to a real environment file, fill in the blank values, and keep or change the model names.
inputs: Values the developer types in: the database address, the AI provider choice, and the Gemini and OpenAI keys.
outputs: Nothing runs from this file. The app reads the values from its environment.
risks: Real keys must never be committed. The allowed values for AI_EXTRACTION_PROVIDER are not listed here, and the code that reads it is not in this packet.
debug: If AI extraction fails, check that DATABASE_URL is set, that the provider name matches what the code expects, that the matching key is filled in, and that the model name is valid.
